item.title: Washington Capitals star Alex Ovechkin crashes a couple's wedding photo shoot on a hotel staircase
item.description: Video captures Alex Ovechkin casually strolling into a couple's wedding photo shoot in Saint Petersburg with a CCM hockey stick in his hands.
item.content:encoded:
When couples take wedding pictures, they usually want to get as many as they can of just the two of them.

But, on the off chance an NHL legend happens to come wandering through the frame, well, you might as well get that photographer you're paying by the hour to start snapping.

That's what one couple in Russia did when none other than the NHL's all-time leading goal-scorer, Alex Ovechkin, happened to stumble upon their photo sesh.

The Great 8 was in his native Russia this offseason, and there, he took part in a charity game called the Match of the Year that included a bunch of familiar names from the NHL and KHL.

In fact, this year, Philadelphia Flyers forward Matvei Michkov scored a slick Michigan move goal that made the rounds on social media.

Anyway, while he was in Saint Petersburg for this match, Ovechkin found himself strolling down a hotel staircase, where a nice couple just so happened to be getting some photos taken to commemorate their big day.

Easily the best part of that video is when you see the blade of the hockey stick come into frame and you know what's about to happen. It's like when Kramer would come sliding through the door and into Jerry's apartment.

Also, the fact that he was just wandering around with a CCM twig in his hands is just perfect in general.

That's how you become an elite goal-scorer, kids: cart the lumber with you just about everywhere.

Ovechkin will be headed back to the States in a little over a month for the Capitals' training camp.

He spent last season on what some thought might be his final year in the NHL, but signed a one-year deal with the Capitals earlier this month.

While the Capitals missed the playoffs last season, they brought in some key pieces over the summer, including former Buffalo Sabres forward Alex Tuch, former St. Louis Blues forward Jordan Kyrou, and former Blue Jackets captain Boone Jenner.

item.title: Chiefs coordinator Eric Bieniemy's son won't face court until mental health evaluation after shooting mother
item.description: Elijah Bieniemy's public defender argues he suffers from significant mental health issues after allegedly shooting his mother Mia at their Ashburn home.
item.content:encoded:
Elijah Bieniemy, the son of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, won’t make a court appearance until he has completed a mental-health competency evaluation, court records show.

The 27-year-old was arrested on Monday after shooting his mother, Mia, who suffered "multiple gunshot wounds" at their home in Ashburn, Virginia on Sunday.

Elijah was arrested on charges of malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony, and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling, the Loudon County Sheriff’s Office said in a press release.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

A new court filing has Elijah’s public defender arguing the client "appears to suffer from significant mental health issues," according to The Athletic.

The filing also said Elijah "does not appear able to assist in his own defense at the present time."

ERIC BIENIEMY SON JAILED FOR SHOOTING HIS MOTHER WHILE KANSAS CITY CHIEFS COACH IS AWAY AT TRAINING CAMP

The mental-health competency evaluation has reportedly been granted, while a motion for a request for a mental-health evaluation was temporarily withdrawn.

Elijah’s preliminary hearing is now set for Sept. 9 — days before the Chiefs take on the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football" to begin the 2026 NFL season.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid gave an update on Mia on Wednesday while addressing the media, saying "she’s doing great."

"She’s doing better and great from where she was," Reid said at training camp. "Out of the ICU unit, happy about that. EB is still with her, that part’s important."

After the arrest, Elijah was transported to Loudon County Adult Detention Center, where he is currently being held without bond.

The Chiefs coaches and team are set to report to camp at Missouri Western State’s campus this Friday, with veterans having already reported on Tuesday.

The 56-year-old Bieniemy returned to the Chiefs as their offensive coordinator this offseason following time with the Washington Commanders, Chicago Bears and UCLA’s football squad in collegiate ball.

As offensive coordinator in Kansas City from 2018-22, Bieniemy oversaw one of the league's most productive offenses to become an AFC stalwart, winning two Super Bowls in his tenure.

OutKick’s Armando Salguero and Fox News’ Ryan Morik contributed to this report.

item.title: Father who bought AR-15 for Georgia school shooter learns fate in first-of-its-kind conviction
item.description: Colin Gray was sentenced to 15 years after a jury found he gave his son the AR-15 used in the Apalachee High School shooting despite mental health warnings.
item.content:encoded:
Colin Gray, the father of Apalachee High School shooter Colt Gray, was sentenced Thursday to 15 years in prison after a Georgia judge said he "failed as a parent" by ignoring escalating warning signs before the 2024 school massacre.

Barrow County Superior Court Judge Nicholas Primm sentenced Gray, 55, to concurrent prison terms after telling him "the warning lights were flashing brighter and brighter" before the shooting and that he failed to remove his son's access to guns or get him needed mental health treatment.

"It is clear you failed as a parent," Primm said before handing down the sentence. "The weight of your crimes is tethered and tied to the acts of someone else, your son."

A jury convicted Colin Gray in March on 27 counts, including second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter, after prosecutors argued he gave his son the AR-15-style rifle used in the attack despite mounting concerns about the teen's mental health. He is the first parent of a school shooter to be convicted of murder.

FORMER VIRGINIA ASSISTANT PRINCIPAL ON TRIAL AFTER ALLEGEDLY IGNORING WARNINGS BEFORE 6-YEAR-OLD SHOT TEACHER

The sentencing came after Colt Gray pleaded guilty to all 55 charges against him and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

During Thursday's hearing, victims' family members urged the judge to impose the maximum sentence, describing the lasting pain caused by the Sept. 4, 2024, shooting.

NEW VIDEO SHOWS OKLAHOMA HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL TACKLING GUNMAN WHO OPENED FIRE INSIDE THE SCHOOL

Shayna Aspinwall, the widow of slain teacher Richard "Ricky" Aspinwall, told the court she suffers from PTSD and is raising the couple's two daughters alone after her husband's death.

"Our daughters must grow up without their father," Aspinwall testified. "They will miss his guidance, his encouragement, his hugs and all the milestones he should have been here to witness — birthdays, graduations, weddings and everyday moments that make up a lifetime will forever be marked by his absence."

She argued that while Colin Gray did not pull the trigger, his failure as a parent and gun owner helped make the tragedy possible.

MAJOR APPEALS COURT DECLARES NEW JERSEY AR-15 BAN UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN LANDMARK SECOND AMENDMENT RULING

In explaining the sentence, Primm said Colin Gray's crimes stemmed from criminal negligence because he failed to intervene despite obvious warning signs. The judge said Colin Gray could have locked the family's guns, removed the ammunition or stored the weapons elsewhere while seeking mental health treatment for his son, telling him that, had he taken those steps, "you wouldn't be here today."

The shooting at Apalachee High School in Barrow County killed teachers Aspinwall, 39, and Cristina Irimie, 53, along with students Mason Schermerhorn and Christian Angulo, both 14. Nine other people were injured.

Prosecutors said Colin Gray ignored warning signs about his son's deteriorating mental health and continued providing him with access to guns, including the AR-15-style rifle authorities said was used in the attack.

Gray is among a small number of U.S. parents criminally charged in a shooting carried out by their children and the first in Georgia.

Friday marks Apalachee High School's first day back for the new school year.

Fox News Digital previously reported that Colt Gray pleaded guilty after initially pleading not guilty to the charges. Before accepting the plea, Judge Primm questioned the teen to ensure he understood the consequences, with Gray responding, "Yes, your honor," to each question.

Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond, Michael Dorgan, The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Carville says one democratic socialist's 'lunacy of the highest level' policy could haunt swing-state Dems
item.description: James Carville warns that democratic socialist candidates in Michigan and Wisconsin primaries could taint the entire Democratic Party's image nationally.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville warned Thursday that far-left candidates winning elections are a liability for the party at the national level.

A wave of democratic socialist candidates winning Democratic primaries in New York City, Abdul El-Sayed's competitive bid for the Democratic nomination for Michigan's U.S. Senate seat and Francesca Hong's frontrunner status in the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor have signaled a significant shift to the left for the party.

On the "Politics War Room" podcast, Carville's co-host, Al Hunt, said that while he disagrees with the narrative that the far-left is ascendant or poised to take over the party, he warned that "it could create problems for other Democrats with a hyped-up narrative that the left is taking over the Democratic Party" and the attention on such candidates "really do pose problems for what otherwise is a good Democratic year."

"I agree, and the problem with Michigan and Wisconsin is what happens in the Michigan Democratic primary doesn't stay in the Michigan Democratic primary," Carville said. "What happens in the Wisconsin Democratic primary for governor doesn't stay in Wisconsin, and they're going to be tagged as part of the Democratic Party," 

SCHUMER DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER DSA BELONGS IN DEMOCRATIC PARTY

While Carville has repeatedly predicted big wins for Democrats in the midterm elections, his mood has somewhat soured in recent months to the point he has proposed a schism to keep the rising far-left flank out of power.

On Thursday, he rhetorically asked democratic socialists, "Why don't you get another name? Why are you dragging our names through the mud with your bulls---? If you don't like it, call yourself something else."

Carville joked that the term "Democratic" can be appropriated even by tyrannical regimes like the Democratic Republic of North Korea and that America’s democratic socialists are genuinely confusing voters.

"If you're so against everything, then create your own name. Don't use our name. Don't be tainted," Carville exclaimed. "But I got to tell you, I hope that voters in the primaries in Michigan and Wisconsin understand you're not just voting for a nominee for Senate in Michigan. 

"You're not just voting for a nominee for governor of Wisconsin. You're voting on the image of the entire party, and there's a lot at stake here. And this is not time for a vanity vote. Not at all. And that's what this is — a vanity vote and nothing more."

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’

Hunt responded by recalling that, after the death of George Floyd in 2020, some Democrats embraced the agenda of defunding the police, which enabled the Republicans to paint the entire party with that agenda. He warned that the same could happen with this new wave of democratic socialists’ far-left ideas.

Carville argued that one key policy from Hong would represent "lunacy of the highest level" to the point it would be a liability for other Democratic candidates when Republicans grill them over it.

"The problem we face right now in Wisconsin: This candidate doesn't want to defund the police. She wants to abolish the police," Carville warned. "So, if we had a Republican gubernatorial nominee in the state of, I don't know, Colorado, pick a state, Tennessee — that was advocating lunacy of this level ... and this is lunacy of the highest level you can imagine ... we would be totally justified in taking that message nationally.

"We would be totally justified in saying you've got to ask these people when they make an appearance if they agree with this," he continued. "Well, they're going to do that to us. And I got to say, you go to a person in a tight race — you go to Roy Cooper, you go to Jon Ossoff, you go to Troy Jackson — and you say, ‘Your nominee in Wisconsin said this. What do you answer?’ That's not a chicken-s--- question at all. And you're just opening yourself up for all of that crap."

Fox News Digital contacted Hong and El-Sayed for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

item.title: Jessica Simpson celebrates turning 46 in bikini and reveals her children have never seen her perform

The singer marked the occasion with a close-up selfie showing her tanning in a black-and-white polka-dot bikini, simply captioning the photo, "💫46💫 July 10/26."

Simpson reclined beneath a purple crocheted cover while wearing oval dark sunglasses. Her blonde hair was styled in a loose side braid, and she accessorized the polka-dot bikini with layered turquoise bead necklaces, a square green pendant, dangling stone earrings and stacked bracelets.

With the sun illuminating her face, the "With You" singer completed the birthday look with glossy lips and a relaxed expression.

item.title: Hamas agrees to complete disarmament under 'historic' Gaza agreement: Trump
item.description: President Donald Trump announced what he called a historic agreement to completely disarm Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza as part of a broader peace initiative.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced a historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza.

The diplomatic breakthrough, brokered by his Board of Peace alongside mediators Egypt, Qatar and Turkey, will pave the way for a new Palestinian government in Gaza, Trump said. 

"Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY," Trump said in a Truth Social post. 

HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL

The agreement represents a "major milestone" in implementing Trump’s 20-Point Plan, a framework introduced last year aimed at ending the war and rebuilding Gaza.

The president said the multiphased disarmament agreement marks a "critical step" toward Gaza being governed by a new Palestinian government with the support of the Board of Peace. 

He added the city will no longer be used as "a base for terror attacks." 

A new police force will also be established in Gaza with the support of the International Stabilization Force, keeping the region "safe for its residents and its neighbors." 

ISRAEL'S MILITARY ELIMINATES HAMAS TERRORIST WHO HELPED ABDUCT AMERICAN-ISRAELI HOSTAGE, 3 OTHERS

Israeli forces will withdraw from the region as the disarmament process moves forward through the structured phases. 

Trump praised the progress his administration has made since Hamas-led militants carried out a deadly assault on southern Israel from the Gaza Strip Oct. 7, 2023.

"One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity. We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do," Trump said. "The threat that emerged from Gaza on October 7 will NOT be allowed to rebuild!

"Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE."

Trump further thanked all the parties involved in the historic agreement. 

"I want to thank the mediators — Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye — for their important efforts, and especially my outstanding team, whose tireless work made this historic breakthrough possible."

item.title: Hiker's unexplained death exposes deadly alcohol withdrawal risk many don't recognize
item.description: Alcohol withdrawal seizures can strike 24 to 48 hours after the last drink, turning wilderness settings into life-threatening traps for heavy drinkers.
item.content:encoded:
When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in California’s Ventana Wilderness, initial speculation pointed to foul play, according to a press release from the Monterey County Sheriff's Office.

However, official coroner's reports revealed her cause of death to be probable alcohol withdrawal seizures brought on by chronic alcohol use disorder.

Friends who were hiking with Shields said she had gone to the river that morning. A short time later, one of them found her unresponsive in the water, according to reports.

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

"This is a probable seizure that occurred as a result of chronic alcohol use disorder, but there was nothing that stood out that indicated any type of criminal activity," Andres Rosas, commander and the primary public information officer for the Monterey County Sheriff's Office, told KSBW 8.

Given the results of the investigation and forensic examination, no further investigation is taking place.

The incident highlights a little-known danger of severe alcohol dependence, as suddenly stopping alcohol can trigger life-threatening neurological events.

Alcohol acts as a depressant on the central nervous system. When someone drinks heavily over a prolonged period, the brain adapts by ramping up chemical signals to keep bodily systems functioning, according to experts.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

When alcohol is abruptly stopped, that blocker on the central nervous system is removed. The brain then enters a state of dangerous overexcitation, leading to severe hyperarousal.

Withdrawal symptoms typically begin within six to 24 hours after the last drink, with the risk of seizures peaking between 24 and 48 hours.

In wilderness settings or isolated locations, a sudden seizure can result in immediate loss of consciousness, trauma, respiratory arrest or an inability to seek emergency care, experts note.

Clinical guidelines from the National Institutes of Health categorize alcohol withdrawal by the following key progression stages.

This may include minor withdrawal symptoms, including insomnia, tremors, anxiety, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis (excessive sweating), heart palpitations, anorexia, nausea, tachycardia (abnormally fast resting heart rate) and hypertension.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

This stage is marked by visual, auditory or tactile hallucinations.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

People in this stage may experience sudden loss of consciousness accompanied by severe muscle contractions (seizures). Another potential symptom is delirium tremens, a medical emergency involving extreme agitation, fever, racing heart, hyperthermia and cardiac instability.

Health agencies, including the National Institutes of Health, strongly advise that individuals with a history of heavy drinking or prior withdrawal episodes never attempt to detox alone or in remote settings.

Medical detox programs use tailored medication protocols to safely taper brain activity and prevent seizures.

Help is available for people struggling with alcohol use disorder. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration National Helpline provides free, confidential treatment referrals 24 hours a day at 1-800-662-4357.

item.title: Saints lock up Chris Olave with 4-year extension worth $132M after training camp hold-in
item.description: Chris Olave's $132 million extension makes him one of the NFL's highest-paid receivers, surpassing Michael Thomas' record Saints deal from 2019.
item.content:encoded:
New Orleans Saints star receiver Chris Olave agreed to a four-year extension worth $132 million with $90 million guaranteed, sources confirmed to OutKick’s Armando Salguero.

Olave was set to play the 2026 NFL season on his fifth-year option, and he was a hold-in at training camp because of it. He wanted a new deal before taking part in practices.

The Saints decided to reward their 2022 first-rounder with his desired extension before potential free agency in 2027.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Olave will remain a cornerstone piece for the franchise alongside new starting quarterback Tyler Shough, who was drafted in the second round in 2025.

This deal marks the highest the Saints have dished out to a receiver since Michael Thomas received a five-year pact worth up to $20 million per season in 2019. At the time, it was a record.

DRAKE LONDON SIGNS $141M DEAL WITH FALCONS, BECOMING THIRD HIGHEST-PAID RECEIVER IN NFL: REPORTS

Olave will be making $33 million per season, cementing him as one of the highest-paid receivers in the NFL.

The Ohio State product earned that during his rookie deal with the Saints, especially last season. In 16 games, Olave notched career highs in yards (1,163), touchdowns (nine) and receptions (100).

Olave started thriving once Shough took over as the team’s starting quarterback, quickly finding chemistry with his new signal-caller, and the Saints clearly believe that connection will lead them to playoff glory once more.

The Saints have not reached the playoffs since the 2020 campaign, though they have sprinkled in 9-8 seasons in there. However, they’ve gone 11-23 the past two seasons, and head coach Kellen Moore’s first year ended at 6-11.

But there were positives that came out of the lackluster record, with the offense being the main highlight. The Saints are excited to see what Shough can do with a full offseason understanding he’s the starting quarterback as well as working more in Moore’s system.

Olave benefited from that system, and the Saints bolstered their offensive weapons by signing Travis Etienne Jr. to their backfield. 

With Saints legend Alvin Kamara returning for another season, the running back depth chart is filled with explosive playmakers, while Olave, tight end Juwan Johnson and 2026 first-round pick Jordan Tyson out of Arizona State have this group primed for success.

item.title: Schiff-backed candidate abruptly ends gubernatorial campaign amid rumblings of a damaging report
item.description: Mandela Barnes suspended his Wisconsin gubernatorial campaign amid a crowded Democratic primary, leaving Francesca Hong and David Crowley as major contenders.
item.content:encoded:
Mandela Barnes, who served as lieutenant governor of Wisconsin from 2019 to 2023, suspended his gubernatorial campaign Thursday, citing a lack of support to capture the Democratic Party nomination.

"It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be," Barnes said in a video statement.

"While I may be suspending my campaign, I’ll never give up my fight for Wisconsin."

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’

Barnes, who was endorsed by Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as the "kind of bold leader we need to take on the Trump administration," did not name the candidate he believes will capture the party’s nomination later this month.

His departure from the race comes as a surprise amid a crowded Democratic field to fill the empty seat of outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers. Barnes was considered a frontrunner in the race because of his proximity to Evers and his name recognition. 

It also coincides with rumblings that Barnes may have abused his position in the past to make sexual advances toward women in the workplace, an allegation currently under investigation by The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, which published its report shortly after Barnes' video post.

Barnes' campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether his decision to suspend the campaign was in any way connected to the reporting. However, a Barnes spokesperson told Politico "there are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela."

With Barnes’ departure, the remaining major candidates include Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist, and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

TOP DEM HOPEFUL FLIPS SCRIPT AFTER YEARS IN SOCIALIST ORBIT WITH PUZZLING CLAIM

Hong has received backing from a number of nationally recognized progressives, including Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif. She had raised nearly $709,000 as of late June, according to state records.

By comparison, Crowley has secured $250,000 and enjoys the support of a number of local organizations and figures.

Evers, pointedly, endorsed Crowley over Barnes, citing Crowley’s experience.

In his departure video, Barnes urged Democrats to unite against Republicans in the November general election.

"Now, I said from the very beginning when I launched this campaign that the No. 1 goal was taking on and defeating Tom Tiffany to deliver big wins for Democrats up and down the ticket," Barnes said, referring to the presumptive Republican nominee.

"Now it’s our time to come together and focus our efforts on that one goal. We have to do everything to beat Tom Tiffany. This is life or death for Wisconsinites who are losing their healthcare under a Trump administration."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Barnes built his campaign on a platform of increasing taxes on the country’s top earners, freezing energy costs, providing universal childcare and lowering the cost of housing.

The gubernatorial primary will take place Aug. 11.

item.title: Toddler's tragic death sparks manslaughter charges after alleged poisoning
item.description: Police say the toddler's lips turned blue, and she suffered a seizure after ingesting kratom pills, but neither adult called 911 or sought medical care.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida father and the mother of his children are behind bars after police said they failed to seek emergency care when a 2-year-old girl turned blue, suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally after allegedly ingesting kratom pills.

Jerome Jonathon Jordan, 35, and Charlene Rea O'Connell, 32, were both charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and child neglect causing great bodily harm in the death of 2-year-old Jonnie Jordan, according to the West Melbourne Police Department.

The charges come more than two months after Jonnie was rushed to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne May 18. 

Hospital staff pronounced the toddler dead shortly after she arrived.

STEPDAD ACCUSED OF SEX ASSAULT AS COPS WIDEN PROBE INTO GIRL’S LETHAL BENADRYL INGREDIENT DOSE

Investigators said the tragedy unfolded the night before at O'Connell's Palm Bay home, where Jonnie allegedly got into kratom pills belonging to Jordan and O'Connell.

Police said they believe the toddler consumed as many as 2½ pills before both adults realized what had happened.

According to investigators, Jordan and O'Connell watched as Jonnie's lips turned blue, she suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally. But instead of calling 911 or taking the little girl to a hospital, police allege they failed to seek medical care.

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

Authorities said Jordan then drove Jonnie back to his sister's apartment in West Melbourne and put her to bed.

Hours later, after waking up and finding the toddler unresponsive, Jordan rushed her to the hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.

Investigators said Jordan initially urged hospital staff to administer Narcan, leading detectives to suspect an overdose early in the investigation.

SHARON STONE'S TERRIFYING WEED WITHDRAWAL SPARKS WARNING ABOUT TODAY'S POTENT MARIJUANA

The Brevard County Medical Examiner's Office determined Jonnie died of acute mitragynine intoxication, according to police.

According to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, part of the National Institutes of Health, kratom is a herbal substance made from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and is commonly sold in powders, capsules, gummies and drinks.

Some people use it for its stimulant or pain-relieving effects, though federal health officials have repeatedly warned about its safety.

While kratom remains legal under federal law, the Drug Enforcement Administration announced earlier this month it had begun the process of temporarily placing high-potency 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products and certain related synthetic compounds into Schedule I, citing their high potential for abuse and opioid-like effects. The action does not apply to natural kratom leaf products.

Following the medical examiner's findings and a months-long investigation, police arrested Jordan and O'Connell Thursday. Both are being held without bond at the Brevard County Jail.

Police said Jordan's sister, whose apartment Jonnie was taken to after leaving O'Connell's home, is not facing any charges.

item.title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti roasts the SEC as ESPN starts their promotional campaign already: 'we don't whine'
item.description: Curt Cignetti fired back at SEC coaches and Greg Sankey at Big Ten media days, calling out the hype machine around strength of schedule excuses.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war of words and messaging is already ramping up.

The SEC this year moves to nine conference games, a large shift that will necessarily impact win-loss records and takes away one of their biggest advantages over the Big Ten or other nine-game conferences. As a result, at SEC media days recently, several coaches and even conference commissioner Greg Sankey started their promotional and excuse campaign for the College Football Playoff.

Despite not reaching the National Championship game for three straight seasons and going 2-7 in the playoff against other Power 4 conference teams, the SEC has started their campaign by saying that they deserve more teams in the tournament. Why? Because of their depth and strength of schedule.

SEC WANTS MORE PLAYOFF FAVORITISM AS GREG SANKEY COMPLAINS ABOUT 'UNSATISFACTORY' TALKS WITH CFB PLAYOFF

Sure, depth and strength of schedule matters, but winning your games matters too. And that's where the SEC coaches and Sankey are going through a bit of a contradictory crisis.

When the SEC was dominant, winning title after title, the narrative went that the depth meant that their teams were battle hardened by playoff time. Other conferences didn't progress through the regular season gauntlet of SEC teams, making them less prepared at the end of the year.

Now that the SEC has fallen behind the Big Ten and are moving to nine conference games, the narrative-building has changed. Just listen to ESPN's Laura Rutledge make excuses for a season and schedule that hasn't happened yet.

LANE KIFFIN MAKES RIDICULOUS EXCUSES FOR SEC'S POOR RECENT PERFORMANCE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

"So, I think one of the reasons why the SEC may not have advanced as far in the playoffs as some SEC fans would like to see," Rutledge told Pat McAfee recently. "It's because the competition within the league is so difficult that nine games of craziness week in and week out are little different than other parts of other conferences. I'm not dissing on the Big 10.

"By the time they get to the end, there are not many left. For one, they eliminate each other, but furthermore, they're gassed. They're injured. They have issues. I'm not making excuses. I'm just pointing out facts because you were pointing out facts," she continued.

"I'm not making excuses," then makes excuses. Because ESPN is heavily invested in promoting the SEC, as their biggest media partners.

First, we have yet to see what a nine-game schedule does to the SEC. Second, implying that the previous eight-game schedule was just too much for these teams to handle is actually an argument against the strength of the conference. Third, what happened to the SEC being so battle hardened they could handle the rigors of a playoff run? Now they're just too tired.

Let's look at the 2024 Ohio State National Championship team as a counterpoint, shall we? The Buckeyes in 2024 had road games at Oregon, ranked No. 3 in the country at the time, and Penn State, which was also then ranked No. 3. It hosted No. 5 Indiana and finished with an always tough, physical, rivalry game against a solid Michigan team. It played three playoff teams in the regular season, including the No. 1 overall seed, Oregon, and another physical opponent in Iowa. All within seven weeks. Sounds pretty tough!

They then blew out a vaunted SEC team, Tennessee, 42-17, easily handled another top SEC team, Texas, and beat a very good Notre Dame team in the championship game. That's what good teams do. Indiana in 2025 played Ohio State to finish the season, then blew out Alabama, Oregon, and handled Miami to win a title. That's what good teams do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Stop making excuses and win important games.

Speaking of excuses and Indiana, if there's one head coach who hates them more than anyone, it's Curt Cignetti. The defending champ took a very pointed shot at the SEC and the excuses culture they've created.

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said on Thursday at Big Ten media days. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Ouch.

Though, to be fair to the SEC, Notre Dame's in the Midwest and boy oh boy did they cry a river, whine, and complain after getting left out of the playoff last season.

He has a point though, about the current strategy around the SEC. For some reason, instead of saying, "hey, we believe we're the best, we'll go through whatever gauntlet we have in front of us, and beat people up in the playoff, because we're the best," they're saying "woe is us, it's just too tough to win games."

Maybe that's the reason the SEC has fallen behind, because they're consumed with talking about the difficult of playing road games at Mississippi State instead of Nebraska. Or Kentucky instead of Wisconsin. Maybe focus on winning, it's a guarantee the rest will take care of itself.

item.title: Chris Hemsworth shares terrifying footage from 'crazy' plane ride through lightning and severe turbulence
item.description: Video from Chris Hemsworth's Costa Rica family vacation captures a terrifying lightning storm mid-flight that he called a "crazy" moment.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Hemsworth's latest family vacation took a frightening turn when the actor found himself aboard a small plane caught in the middle of a lightning storm.

On Wednesday, the "Thor" star, 42, captured the Costa Rican family trip with wife Elsa Pataky and their three children in a YouTube vlog, including a "life-threatening" plane ride. 

Footage from the trip captured lightning flashing around the aircraft as turbulence shook the cabin. Hemsworth's unease was evident in the clip, as he could be seen mouthing, "What the f---?"

In the caption of the video, Hemsworth also called it a "crazy plane ride."

CHRIS HEMSWORTH SHUTS DOWN CLAIMS ALZHEIMER'S FEARS FORCED HIM TO QUIT HOLLYWOOD: 'REALLY... P---ED ME OFF'

The flight landed safely, and the scare didn't stop the Hemsworth family from making the most of the vacation.

The action-packed trip featured everything from surfing and ATV riding to cliff jumping, fishing and hiking through waterfalls. At one point, Pataky playfully shoved her husband into a waterfall.

CHRIS HEMSWORTH, BRAD PITT, BEN AFFLECK ARE AMONG MALE STARS GETTING BETTER WITH AGE: PHOTOS

The couple, who married in 2010, share daughter India and twin sons Sasha and Tristan. The family has long embraced an adventurous lifestyle, frequently sharing glimpses of outdoor excursions from their home in Australia and while traveling abroad.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The vacation scare comes several years after Hemsworth publicly revealed he was rethinking how he approached work and family after a health revelation during filming of National Geographic's "Limitless."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

While undergoing genetic testing for the series, the actor learned he carries two copies of the APOE4 gene, which is linked to an increased risk of developing Alzheimer's disease later in life.

Shortly after the news was made public in 2022, he took a break from acting. Together, the two bits of news led to rumors that he was retiring, or that he'd already developed the disease, which he said was very upsetting to hear.

"It really kind of p---ed me off because it felt like I had been vulnerable with something personal and shared this," he admitted in an interview with Vanity Fair in 2024.

"No matter how much I said, ‘This is not a death sentence,’ the story became that I have dementia, and I’m reconsidering life and retiring and so on."

He then joked, "I did read a really funny comment at the bottom of one article: ‘I hope Chris forgets he’s retiring and comes back.’"

Fox News Digital's Emily Trainham contributed to this post.

item.title: NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has simple advice for Caitlin Clark: 'Keep shutting up the haters'
item.description: NFL legend Rob Gronkowski had high praise and simple advice for Caitlin Clark as the discourse about the Indiana Fever star has continued to rage on.
item.content:encoded:
NFL legend Rob Gronkowski had high praise and some simple advice for Caitlin Clark: "Keep shutting up the haters" with her play.

Amid the rampant discourse about Clark that has dominated the internet, Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview she’s doing a "great job" of handling it all.

"She's doing a great job handling herself. She really is. I'm not in her shoes. I'm not in her situation. If I was, though, I would kind of handle it very similar to how she's handling it. She really is doing a great job," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I would just say one piece of advice: Keep balling because if you keep balling, you're going to keep shutting up the haters."

The Indiana Fever have won their last four games, and Clark has been averaging just over 30 points per game during that winning streak. While Clark has been good, so have her teammates. Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston have both been key contributors.

Gronkowski praised Clark’s teammates for supporting her throughout the season.

"What I do appreciate, what she's going to need to help with is her teammates. That's who's going to lift you up. If you've got your teammates protecting you, that says a lot right there. It really does. And she does. Her team does pick her up. They protect her as well, and that's huge," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital on behalf of eBay.

NFL LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI DETAILS TRAVIS KELCE AND TAYLOR SWIFT'S 'MAGNIFICENT' WEDDING

"That says a lot about your personality and about who you are throughout the season, how you practice, how you prepare, is that if your teammates are behind you, you know that doing the right things."

Gronkowski said Clark will truly be the face of the WNBA once the league steps in and does something about the hard fouls she has received, in addition to winning something significant.

"I think she's going to be the face eventually, like truly where the WNBA steps in, and they're like, ‘OK, like enough of all this wishwashing that's going on with her and the punishment that she's taking out on the basketball court. Let's truly make her face of the league. I think I would say it once she keeps balling out and also wins something pretty significant," Gronkowski said.

The New England Patriots legend said he isn’t a diehard fan and is more of a casual fan of the WNBA. He talked about how, in the NFL and NBA, you don’t become the face of the league until you have about "four or five years under their belt."

Gronkowski, a four-time Super Bowl champion, is one of the greatest tight ends of all time. He spent nine seasons with the Patriots before retiring in 2019. He came out of retirement in 2020 and played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tom Brady for two seasons before retiring again.

In 11 seasons, the five-time Pro Bowler caught 621 receptions for 9,286 yards and 92 touchdowns.

Clark and the Fever will look to keep it rolling when they play the Portland Fire Friday at 10 p.m. ET.

item.title: Washington school district reviewing incident of employee making celebratory remark about Charlie Kirk's death
item.description: The Lake Washington School District says it launched a review after viral video captured a staff member apparently celebrating Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
A Washington school district says it has launched a review after a woman identified online as a high school nurse appeared in a confrontation that went viral this week about Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. During the dispute, she allegedly said, "Thank God he's dead."

The Lake Washington School District confirmed to Fox News Digital Wednesday it is aware of the video circulating on social media involving a district employee and said it is reviewing the circumstances while emphasizing that the views expressed do not reflect those of the district.

"Lake Washington School District (LWSD) is aware of a video circulating on social media involving a district staff member," a spokesperson for the school district told Fox News Digital in a statement Wednesday. 

"We have received concerns from community members regarding the statements and conduct shown in the video."

OKLAHOMA STATE AGENCY FIRES STAFF ATTORNEY AFTER ANTI-ICE SOCIAL MEDIA TIRADE

In the video shared on X by the account Right Angle News Network, a woman identified in the post as a nurse at Eastlake High School named Kelsey Ballin allegedly says, "Oh my God, thank God he’s dead, bye," after someone else references Charlie Kirk.

She also appears to mockingly blow a kiss, stick out her tongue and give the finger during the incident, which reportedly took place at a farmer's market. Other people in the video were wearing Kirk "Freedom" T-shirts during the incident.

Kirk was assassinated Sept. 10 while speaking at Utah Valley University during his American Comeback Tour.

UTAH VALLEY UNIVERSITY SCRAPS CONTROVERSIAL COMMENCEMENT SPEAKER WHO CRITICIZED CHARLIE KIRK AFTER HIS MURDER

Eastlake High School is part of the Lake Washington School District, located in Sammamish, Washington, and serves grades 9 through 12.

"The district takes these concerns seriously," the spokesperson continued. "While we cannot comment on individual personnel matters, district leadership has initiated a review of the circumstances surrounding this incident and will follow established processes as the review moves forward. It is important to note the views expressed in the video do not reflect the values or positions of Lake Washington School District.

"LWSD is committed to providing welcoming, safe and inclusive learning environments for all students, families, staff and community members. We expect all employees to uphold the professional standards and the values of the district and to contribute to a culture of respect, dignity and civil discourse."

WISCONSIN TEACHER FIRED AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ADVOCATING TO 'MAKE AMERICANS GREAT ASSASSINS AGAIN'

"At the same time," the spokesperson added, "district employees retain rights and protections as private citizens. Balancing these principles is central to how the district approaches situations like this one. Because this is an ongoing personnel matter, we are unable to provide additional information at this time. We remain committed to our values as an organization for developing students that are prepared as members of a diverse community."

When asked about its policies governing employees' conduct outside of work and on social media, the district referred Fox News Digital to its staff conduct policy and separate guidance addressing employees' use of social media.

Fox News Digital reached out to Turning Point USA for comment, and was referred to an X post Thursday from Andrew Kolvet, spokesman for TPUSA, where he reshared the X post from Right Angle News Network and wrote, "Why are so many of these awful humans drawn to children, schools, and medicine?"

Fox News Digital reached out to Ballin for comment.

item.title: Fox News Poll: GOP divisions shape Texas Senate race
item.description: Ken Paxton trails James Talarico by three points in the Texas Senate race as character concerns and a GOP unity gap reshape the 2026 midterm battle.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump won the Lone Star state by nearly 14 percentage points in 2024, but a new Fox News Poll of Texas registered voters suggests this year's Senate race is far less settled. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has yet to fully unify the GOP despite the president’s endorsement in the GOP primary against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

In addition, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve than worry Democratic challenger James Talarico is too extreme, and more Democrats than Republicans are extremely motivated to vote (by 7 points) and extremely interested in the midterms (by 6).

Those dynamics give Talarico a 3-point edge over Paxton (51% vs. 48%) in the Senate contest (within the survey’s margin of sampling error).

Talarico's advantage in the race grows to 6 points among both extremely motivated and extremely interested voters (53% vs. 47% in each group).

FOX NEWS POLL: DEMOCRATIC ENTHUSIASM SHAPES NORTH CAROLINA SENATE RACE

Most independents (68%) and virtually all Democrats support Talarico (98%), while fewer Republicans are unified behind Paxton (89%).

In part, that’s because one quarter of non-MAGA Republicans back Talarico (24%).

Paxton is the choice among White evangelical Christians, White men without a college degree, rural voters, regular worship attenders, men and voters ages 65 and older.

Some of Talarico’s best groups are Black voters, moderates, voters under age 30, Hispanic voters, women and voters with a college degree.

"Although Paxton dominated Cornyn in the GOP primary, that bruising contest left scars," said Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts Fox News polls with Democrat Chris Anderson. 

"He has considerable work to do with non-MAGA Republicans and independents, and that undoubtedly requires aggressively tying Talarico to the Democratic Party’s far left." 

By a 12-point margin, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve as a senator than believe Talarico is too extreme (59% vs. 47%).

Twice as many Republicans are concerned about Paxton's character as Democrats are that Talarico is too extreme (36% vs. 17%).

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

Still, about 8 in 10 Paxton and Talarico supporters say their backing is more about where the candidates stand on the issues than who they are as people. 

Trump received a 55% favorable vs. 44% unfavorable rating in the 2024 Texas Fox News Voter Analysis (FNVA) election survey. Today, those numbers have flipped: 45% favorable vs. 54% unfavorable, for a minus-9 net negative rating.

Paxton garners a minus-6 net personal rating, 45% favorable vs. 51% unfavorable, while Talarico is in positive territory by 6 points, 49% vs. 43%.

Talarico is more popular than the Democratic Party while the GOP edges out Paxton. 

While both parties are viewed negatively, the GOP is underwater by only 2 points (48% favorable vs. 50% unfavorable), compared with the Democratic Party at minus-9 (45% vs. 54%).

Despite Texas being a border state, nearly 4 in 10 say inflation will be the most important issue to their Senate vote, while 2 in 10 say immigration and 1 in 10 say healthcare, political divisions and unemployment.

By more than a 2-to-1 margin, Texas voters say they are falling behind financially rather than getting ahead (35% vs. 16%). Half are holding steady.

In the race for governor, incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott is favored by 1 point over Democrat Gina Hinojosa.

Part of Abbott's edge comes from a touch more crossover support: 12% of Talarico supporters back Abbott, while 9% of Paxton supporters back Hinojosa.

Hinojosa has the advantage among extremely motivated (+6) and extremely interested voters (+5).

Abbott has a net positive personal rating by a single point (50% favorable vs. 49% unfavorable). Hinojosa is in positive territory by 11 points (45% vs. 34%), although nearly 1 in 5 are unable to rate her.

Texas last elected a Democratic governor in 1990 (Ann Richards), a Democratic Senator in 1988 (Lloyd Bentsen), and a Democratic presidential candidate in 1976 (Jimmy Carter).

A closer look at the Hispanic electorate

Hispanic voters say their Senate pick will be driven by inflation, as roughly 4 in 10 say it will be the most important issue to their vote and another 4 in 10 say they’re falling behind financially. This mostly matches views among all Texas voters.

And as is the case with voters overall, there is an enthusiasm gap, as more Hispanic Democrats than Hispanic Republicans are interested and motivated to vote in the midterms.

Overall, Hispanic voters prefer Talarico by 18 points (59% vs. 41%).

Some 9% of Hispanic GOP voters crossover to support Talarico while 5% of Hispanic Democrats favor Paxton.

CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE

In 2024, Trump topped former Vice President Kamala Harris among Hispanic voters in Texas by 1 point, according to the Texas FNVA survey (49% Harris vs. 50% Trump).

By 20 points, more Hispanic voters are concerned that Paxton lacks the character to serve as senator than feel Talarico is too extreme (61% concerned vs. 41%).

For the governor’s race, Hispanic voters back Hinojosa by 16 points in the new survey. By comparison, they preferred Beto O’Rourke over Abbott by 14 points in 2022.

More than half of Hispanic voters view Talarico (57% favorable), Hinojosa (53%), and the Democratic Party (53%) positively, while more than half have negative views of Paxton (56% unfavorable), Abbott (56%), Trump (61%), and the Republican Party (59%).

Conducted July 23-27, 2026, under the direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News survey includes interviews with a sample of 1,006 Texas registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (72) and cellphones (681) or completed the survey online after receiving a text (253). Results based on the full sample have a margin of sampling error of ±3 percentage points. 

The survey includes an oversample of 296 Hispanic voters, bringing the sample size for that subgroup to 556 (±4). Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling errors, question wording and order can influence results. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics are representative of the registered voter population. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data.

item.title: Pentagon fires back after Mark Kelly accuses Pete Hegseth of targeting women and Black military officers
item.description: The Department of War rejected Sen. Mark Kelly's claims that Pete Hegseth targeted women and Black officers, citing merit-based promotion policies.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of War (DOW) rejected Sen. Mark Kelly's allegations Thursday that War Secretary Pete Hegseth targeted women and Black military officers because of their identities. 

In a statement to Fox News Digital responding to Kelly's interview on "Next Question with Katie Couric," the department pointed to statements from two Pentagon spokesmen maintaining that military promotions were based on merit, not race and gender.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the department would not use a service member's identity when making promotion decisions.

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES

"As we’ve said before, military promotions are given to those who have earned them. The Department will never consider the color of a service member’s skin or their gender as a factor in promotions," Parnell said in one of the statements cited by the department to Fox News Digital.

"Under President Trump and @SecWar Hegseth, meritocracy reigns supreme at the War Department."

"They also fire women, and they fire Black people because of their gender and the color of their skin," he told Couric. "They've done that repeatedly. They don't even try to make excuses about it. They just fire them."

Kelly, a retired Navy captain and member of the Armed Services Committee, previously accused Hegseth of removing former Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. CQ Brown because of his race in an appearance Sunday on MS NOW's "PoliticsNation." President Donald Trump fired Brown shortly after taking office again in 2025.

The Arizona Democrat also pointed to the removal of Adm. Lisa Franchetti, the first woman to serve as chief of naval operations, accusing Hegseth of blocking promotions and removing officers because of their race or gender. Kelly said the personnel changes would deprive the military of experienced leaders.

HEGSETH SAYS PENTAGON WILL REVIEW MARK KELLY'S PUBLIC STATEMENTS ABOUT CLASSIFIED BRIEFING AMID ONGOING FEUD

"We’re losing a generation of leaders because there will be women and Black people that’ll say, ‘Well, I don’t feel like I have opportunity here anymore. I’m just going to leave mid-career instead of staying.’ So, we’ll lose some of our best people," Kelly told Couric. 

Acting Pentagon press secretary Joel Valdez also rejected the premise that the department's personnel decisions were discriminatory. The DOW directed Fox News Digital to his statement as part of its response to Kelly's allegations.

"Here’s the bottom line: anyone who has an issue with merit-based promotions should reconsider their values. Promotions based solely on race and gender is wrong," Valdez said on X last month.

AIR FORCE RESCINDING 135 PROMOTIONS AFTER TEST SCORING ERROR: 'THIS IS GOING TO BE HARD'

Trump dismissed Brown in February 2025 and selected retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Dan "Razin" Caine to replace him. 

Hegseth separately requested nominees to replace Franchetti, Air Force Vice Chair of Staff Gen. Jim Slide and the judge advocate general of the Army, Navy and Air Force during a broader Pentagon leadership shake-up.

Military officials questioned whether women and minority officers had been singled out because of their identities, an allegation Pentagon officials strongly disputed. The department did not publicly disclose its specific rationale for the removals.

Hegseth has maintained that promotions should be determined by performance rather than identity. During a September address to senior military leaders at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, he described identity-based advancement as a form of poor leadership.

"Real toxic leadership is promoting people based on immutable characteristics or quotas instead of based on merit," Hegseth said.

Fox News Digital's Michael Lee contributed to this report.

item.title: Former Auburn two-way star Bobby Hunt, Chiefs Super Bowl I starter, dead at 85
item.description: Bobby Hunt led the AFL with 10 interceptions the year he started at safety for the Kansas City Chiefs in their Super Bowl I loss to Green Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Bobby Hunt, a former do-it-all football standout for the Auburn Tigers, has died. He was 85.

The Alabama Sports Hall of Fame, which inducted Hunt in 2015, confirmed his death. "Our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends," the hall wrote in a tribute shared to Facebook.

Details on Hunt's cause of death were not immediately made public.

At Lanett High School in Alabama, Hunt played quarterback and defensive back. He also spent time at both the punter and punt returner positions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

He took that all-around talent to Auburn, where he continued to play quarterback and safety.

Hunt was coached by Ralph "Shug" Jordan at Auburn. According to AL.com, Hunt's talent was noticed by Auburn's top rival. Famed former Alabama coach Paul "Bear" Bryant once described Hunt as "just a great football player — that’s all."

After his two-way college football career, Hunt was picked by the Dallas Texans in the 11th round of the 1962 American Football League draft.

Once he reached the professional ranks, Hunt focused strictly on safety. He recorded eight interceptions as a rookie and earned first-team All-AFL honors before the Texans relocated to Kansas City, Missouri, in 1963 and became the Chiefs.

Three seasons later, Hunt was in the starting lineup when the Chiefs faced the Green Bay Packers in the first Super Bowl.

Hunt finished his professional football career with a two-season stint with the expansion Cincinnati Bengals.

Hunt appeared in 112 games as a pro, finishing his career with 42 interceptions. After his playing days ended, Hunt joined the coaching ranks as an assistant with the Buffalo Bills.
